title: Full Tank Dey Burn Slow?

dayo.name: DAYO
dayo.role: Tops up N10k at a time

tobi.name: TOBI
tobi.role: Fills the tank (for the wrong reason)

lines.text: Abeg, ten thousand. Just ten. Economy no dey smile.
Dayo! Every two days you dey here. Me, I fill my tank once, e last me one week!
Na wetin I no understand o! My fuel dey run like say tank get hole.
Na science! When tank full, air no get space inside, so fuel no dey dry off. E dey last!
Tobi, sit down! Tank dey close tight, fuel no dey dry. Na engine dey burn am. Same speed, full or half!
Ten thousand na like seven litres. Small fuel, small distance!
Your gauge too dey play you. E hold Full long time, then fall quick-quick for bottom.
So full tank no dey save fuel?
E no go make fuel burn slow. But e save you trips and queue. And your fuel pump dey sit inside fuel to cool. No dey run am for reserve!
And buy from station wey you trust. Check say meter start from zero!
So I correct, but for wrong reason?
Na so! Full tank no be magic. Na planning!

facts_note: The engine burns fuel at a rate set by driving and engine load, not tank level; a full tank is ~30-40 kg heavier (marginally worse, negligible). N10,000 at ~N1,369/L (NNPC Lagos, late Oct 2026) is ~7.3 L, roughly 60-90 km in city traffic. Fuel gauges are non-linear near Full/Empty. In-tank electric fuel pumps are cooled by surrounding fuel; habitually running near empty can shorten pump life and pull in sediment. Real benefits of filling up: fewer trips/queues, pump protection, buffer during scarcity.
